newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Satellite eyes breakeven cash flow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Satellite eyes breakeven cash flow.

text.p: U.S. Satellite Broadcasting Co's direct broadcast service should reach breakeven cash flow by June 30, 1997, Bernie Weiss, vice president-finance, told Reuters after the company's annual meeting.
Weiss expects the subscriber base -- 1,045,000 at September 30 -- to rise to 1.6 million paying customers by June 30. At that level, he said, "we will reach breakeven cash flow."

Chairman Stanley S. Hubbard said the St. Paul, Minn.-based company welcomes new competition in direct broadcasting. "The introduction of new players (such as the News Corp /MCI Communications Corp planned entry) will expand the market," he said.

Commenting on street expectations for the company, Hubbard said, "Personally, I believe analysts are off the mark. Their (earnings) estimates are low. They don't realize that competition will help, not hurt, because the market will expand."
The First Call consensus on U.S. Satellite, which makes available premium networks to owners of digital satellites, is for a loss of $0.94 per share in fiscal 1997.
